title: LLM-based virtual screening identifies two NIR-II fluorophores tested in vitro and in vivo
summary: Researchers trained a large-language-model framework to predict fluorophore emission wavelengths and used virtual screening to prioritize NIR-II imaging molecules. Two candidates were experimentally characterized and showed favorable imaging performance in vitro and in vivo, according to the abstract. The abstract supplies no quantitative imaging effect sizes. This summary is limited to the abstract and October 15, 2026 publication metadata; the candidates are imaging probes.
ai_technology: Large language model for structure-property prediction, with virtual screening
organization: Shanghai Institute of Materia Medica, Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences; Tianjin University of Traditional Chinese Medicine; Tsinghua Shenzhen International Graduate School; Shandong Laboratory of Yantai Drug Discovery, Bohai Rim Advanced Research Institute For Drug Discovery

evidence.unknown: Source checking does not establish independent confirmation. Review date: 2026-11-15.
